text: To prove 'if n² is even, then n is even', one assumes n is odd and shows n² is odd. Which proof technique is this?
explanation: The argument proves ¬Q ⇒ ¬P, which is logically equivalent to P ⇒ Q. A proof by contradiction would instead assume both that n² is even and that n is odd, then derive ⊥; here the original hypothesis is never assumed.
